Today’s newsletter is brought to you by **[Choose Rich Live](https://www.youtube.com/@chooserichnick/streams)**[!](https://www.youtube.com/@chooserichnick/streams)

Our very own Nick O’Neill is has launched a new stream covering crypto, finance, AI, tech, and the stories shaping the internet economy.

If you already follow Nick, you know what to expect: sharp takes, market chaos, founder brain, and the occasional banger you’ll see clipped on the timeline five minutes later.

Episodes will be streaming live on YouTube, so make sure you’re subscribed to catch the next one as it happens.

**[Subscribe to Choose Rich Live!](https://www.youtube.com/@chooserichnick/streams)**

———————————————————————————

## Top Stories

**BTC** $85,019 (5.7%) | **ETH** $2,721 (5.5%) | **SOL** $117 (7.5%)

* Bitcoin surges [above $85K](https://x.com/KobeissiLetter/status/2101977238883221919) for the first time in 9 months — Over $400M in levered shorts [liquidated](https://x.com/CoinDesk/status/2101967230829199733?s=20) in 4 hours

* Russian Finance Ministry expects up to [10 million new crypto users ](https://x.com/WatcherGuru/status/2101967752575541602)in 2027

* Jack Butcher launches [open edition NFT mint](https://x.com/jackbutcher/status/2101796578428104762?s=20) using X Money

* Uniswap founder says SBF paid [seven figures for Uniswap.com ](https://x.com/TheBlockCo/status/2101958000403763404)after refusal to meet asking price

* Anthropic stealth tests [Opus 5.5 ](https://x.com/testingcatalog/status/2101960963838574608)under codename claude-wafer-eap with possible Tuesday release

* Meta Muse app launches[ AI auto-negotiation](https://x.com/nikitabier/status/2101910604646625710) on Facebook Marketplace

* Zora teases [new CEO](https://x.com/zora/status/2101968708839092255) and possible [big app launch](https://x.com/zora/status/2101960722309644394)

* WLFI opens [150M $WLFI claim](https://x.com/worldlibertyfi/status/2101968345918501185) via Binance with nothing locked

🧠 Crypto News Brief: Bitcoin's breakout to an eight-month high has flipped the mood bullish, but prediction-market integrity questions and North Korean cyber threats remind investors that trust remains crypto's scarcest asset. 🚀 Bitcoin Hits $85K, Its Highest Level Since January Bitcoin pushed to around $85,000 on Monday, its highest level in nearly eight months, as a fourth straight decline in oil prices and hopes for renewed US–Iran diplomacy lifted risk appetite. The move wiped out more than $260 million in short positions within a single hour and followed BTC's first weekly close above its 50-week moving average in 45 weeks — a signal some analysts read as confirmation that the bear-market low is in. Read full story 🎯 Kalshi Faces Wash-Trading Allegations Over Crypto Perps Regulated US prediction market Kalshi is under scrutiny after a quant analyst flagged its ether perpetual futures logging about $539 million in 24-hour volume against roughly $3.1 million in open interest, driven by repetitive, identical $5,500 trades. The critic argued a CFTC-filed near-zero fee schedule incentivizes volume churn; Kalshi's crypto lead rejected the claims, saying its volume reporting follows standard industry convention and that its fees deter manipulation. More details 🚨 WSJ: Polymarket Faced $10M Fraud Attempt Amid Growth Push Fraudsters tried to push at least $10 million through Polymarket's US platform in February using stolen debit cards, with payment processor Checkout.com at one point rejecting more than 80% of deposits as fraudulent versus an industry norm of about 1%, The Wall Street Journal reported. CEO Shayne Coplan reportedly told staff to prioritize growth and deal with regulatory fines later. Polymarket says it has since strengthened its controls, and a Sullivan & Cromwell review concluded the firm complied with regulations. Read more 🕵️ North Korean Fake Recruiters Infect 30K Devices, Steal $10.7M A joint advisory from authorities in Japan, the US, Australia and Germany says North Korea-linked group WaterPlum, also known as Contagious Interview, posed as recruiters for crypto, AI and NFT firms to infect at least 30,000 devices in over 100 countries.
